THE HEADLINE FINDING IS A RETRACTION, recorded here because it is the most useful thing this bead produced: the pattern it was BUILT around does not exist. 'The same content gets re-read' was reported at 18.3% of all cost, headlined by 'one PNG read 8 times = 12% of everything'. Both were artifacts of my own analysis — grouping ran ACROSS sessions (18.3 -> 13.3%), and the fingerprint rendered blocks to TEXT, which images do not have, so 8 DIFFERENT screenshots collided into one fake duplicate group (13.3 -> 1.3%). Each PNG was read once, legitimately, while writing the README. What survives at 1.3% is boilerplate 'file has been updated' acks. Rule deleted, by the same test that rejected error-results (0.1%) and imported cache-thrash (precondition never occurs here; our max parallel calls is 3). The fingerprint FIX was kept — it was a real bug mis-grouping our largest blocks. Specs pin all three rejections so they cannot drift back.
